summary: Intermittent p99 tail-latency spikes on dedicated cluster due to NVLink daisychain contention and long-lived small streams
description: Issue summary: Customer (NexaHealth) reports intermittent p99 tail-latency spikes during sustained traffic windows on their dedicated cluster. Impact: user-facing generation calls observe occasional 5-15s tail latencies causing application timeouts and degraded UX. Hypothesis: contention across NVLink connection chain (daisychain topology) combined with a surge of many long-lived, low-throughput streams is causing backend pipeline stalls and autoscaler misclassification. Environment: dedicated pool with mixed A100-40GB and A100-80GB nodes; placements have resulted in multi-hop NVLink paths for some tenants.
impact: Several customers' requests hit p99 > 10s intermittently; throughput for pinned cluster dipped ~30% during events; customer reports production errors and increased retries leading to higher billable retries and degraded SLOs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route sustained traffic of many small streaming sessions (1-5 tokens per request) for vicuna-13b pinned to the dedicated pool
2) Mix in a few long-lived low-CPU streams (open WS for 10-20s) to simulate chat sessions
3) Observe tail-latency metrics on per-tenant dashboard and GPU perf counters
4) Trigger autoscaler test by artificially increasing ephemeral stream count by ~40% over baseline
observed_logs: Mar 08 11:32:14 node-a gpu-manager: nvlink-transfer latency spike: 12.4ms (baseline 1.1ms)
Mar 08 11:32:15 runtime: batcher: serialize_wait=108ms, prefetch_wait=720ms, kv-cache-lock=1.2s
Mar 08 11:32:16 serving: p99=11234ms, p50=48ms; queue_depth increased from 12 to 84
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support confirmed correlation between small-stream fanout and p99 spikes (see heatmap)
SRE observed NVLink hop counts higher for affected allocations; nodes in same rack showed direct NVLink islands while others required multi-hop transfers
Heap of long-lived WS streams holding KV-caches and preventing effective batching consolidation
Autoscaler logs show repeated allocate/release events for the tenant; heuristics treated slow prefetch as sustained demand causing oscillation
actions_taken: 1) Temporarily applied soft-rate-limit at the tenant edge to cap open streaming sessions (mitigated immediate tail spikes)
2) Rebalanced some of the customer's pinned slots to nodes with single-hop NVLink during peak window (manual placement using scheduler affinity)
3) Restarted gpu-manager sidecar on nodes with highest nvlink-transfer-latency to clear a suspected firmware transporter queue
4) Added detailed trace capture (sampled) for affected tenant to collect batcher and NVLink latencies during next window
proposed_workaround: Keep tenant streaming concurrency capped to 50 connections per shard and prefer single-hop NVLink islands; advise customer to switch to short-lived non-streaming requests for high QPS paths until permanent fix is deployed.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigations applied on 2026-03-09: rate limits and manual rebalancing reduced p99 spikes from >10s to ~600-900ms. Full fix requires scheduler topology-awareness change and autoscaler heuristic update. Patch branch created to prefer balanced NVLink placement and to factor in prefetch stall signals into the autoscaler; PR referenced above. Firmware vendor has been engaged for nvlink transport micro-bug—firmware update scheduled in maintenance window.
next_steps: 1) Backport and release scheduler affinity patch that biases allocations to single-hop NVLink islands (owner: infra/scheduler team) - target 2026-03-17
2) Update autoscaler heuristic to detect long-lived low-throughput streams and avoid upscaling purely on open-session count (owner: autoscale team) - target 2026-03-20
3) Coordinate with hardware vendor for NVLink firmware rollout and validate post-update perf (owner: hwops) - scheduled 2026-03-22
4) Follow up with NexaHealth on client SDK changes to reduce idle streaming if feasible (owner: CS)
5) Create a monitoring alert that fires on nvlink-hop-latency + kv-cache-lock > 500ms to auto-engage SRE
